items.title: Mozambique: Grain Institute explores cooperation opportunities at Trade Expo Indonesia
items.summary: The Mozambique Grain Institute (ICM), represented by its Director-General, Luís Jobe Fazenda, is participating in the 41st edition of Trade Expo Indonesia (TEI), the largest trade and investment platform in Southeast Asia, taking place from 14 to 18 October at the Indonesia Convention Exhibition (ICE), in Greater Jakarta Photo: Instituto de Cereais de Moçambique, IP The ICM is part of the official delegation of the Ministry of Economy, headed by the Secretary of State for Trade, António Grispos As a central player in the agricultural marketing value chain, the ICM is taking part in this global forum to develop cooperation opportunities covering everything from strategic supply to the final marketing of products.

items.title: Mozambique: Government plans to recruit 2,920 more teachers, 598 healthcare workers next year

items.title: Canada to support 200 Mozambican SMEs
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Canadian government, through its initiative “Trade for Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth” (TRISEG), will support 200 Mozambican small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), focusing on strengthening business competitiveness, export capacity, digital transformation and climate resilience. The project, which is expected to cover 60 percent of businesses owned or led by women, is Funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and implemented by TFO Canada in partnership with the Mozambique’s Institute for the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (IPEME). TRISEG is a regional initiative to Empower SMEs in Developing Countries. In Africa, it covers eight countries: Mozambique, Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Nigeria, Senegal and Zambia. Speaking at the project launch ceremony, Pascale Thivierge, Head of Cooperation at the High Commission of Canada in Mozambique, reaffirmed Canada’s commitment to strengthening economic and trade relations with Mozambique.

items.title: Revenue from LNG is for current development and future generations – Finance Minister
items.summary: Maputo, 16 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican Government has stressed that revenue from liquefied natural gas (LNG) production will be used both to finance the country’s current development and to create wealth for future generations. “The Mozambican Government’s objective is indeed to ensure that revenue from natural gas can generate intergenerational wealth. The Sovereign Wealth Fund Law is already producing tangible results by establishing a division of LNG revenue between public expenditure and savings”, said Carla Loveira, Finance Minister. “We do not want all the resources to be entirely consumed by the current budget”, she added. Under the model currently in force, around 60 percent of revenue is channelled to the State Budget, while the remaining 40 percent goes into a savings account managed by the Bank of Mozambique. According to the minister, the funds are already financing major infrastructure projects.

items.title: Albanian protests turn violent: What we know
items.summary: Tirana has seen four days of clashes and the protests are spreading Protesters and anti-riot police have clashed in Albania's main cities in scenes not witnessed for decades Government buildings have been attacked and some private businesses, too Albania's capital Tirana has seen months of protests from an anti-government "Flamingo" movement, but what started on Tuesday this week was on a different scale And the clashes have spread beyond Tirana - to include the main cities of Durrës, Shkodër, Lezhë and Vlora in the west, Gjirokastër in the south and Korçë in the east The new demonstrations were announced as a student movement, ostensibly demanding action by the government to help with the high cost of education fees and books - and the higher cost of living Secondary schools joined in, swelling the numbers Before too long, masked protesters threw stones at police, and they responded with water cannon, tear gas and batons Many were incensed by scenes of a young man being carried away, his broken leg dangling with him in agony Apologies were expressed but failed to calm the situation…

items.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
items.summary: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules? A dispute over Islamic headscarves in Azerbaijani schools has triggered protests at home and an unusual exchange of criticism between politicians in Azerbaijan and Turkey , two countries whose leaders routinely describe their relationship as that of "one nation, two states". The row has raised questions about religious freedom, sovereignty and the limits of Turkish and Iranian influence in the south Caucasian country The unprecedented protests have been taking place across Azerbaijan for a nearly week. Children have demonstrated against the headscarf ban introduced at schools.
